lessons.title: First look
lessons.blurb: Pick a source, orbit the camera, turn up Z Push, and make your first patch.

chapters.text: This is Rutt Etra Web, a browser recreation of the 1973 Rutt Etra scan processor, an analog video synthesizer.
No camera needed for this tour. Click Pattern, and the built-in pattern generator becomes the picture.
The image is drawn as horizontal scan lines. Brighter areas push the lines toward you, so the picture becomes a landscape.
Drag in the render window to orbit the virtual camera around it.
The Controls panel on the right holds every parameter. Type in the search box to find one. Here, Z Push, the depth of the raster.
Drag a knob up to turn it up. More push, deeper relief.
The Patch Bay on the left is the same instrument, laid out as a hardware faceplate. Maximize it to see every jack.
Right-click empty space to add a node. We will add an LFO, a slow oscillator.
Drag from the LFO's output jack onto Z Push's input. The cable is the patch.
Restore the window, and the raster now breathes on its own.
Pick a source, shape it, and patch movement into it. Next, we will learn our way around the windows.

lessons.title: Windows, tabs and layouts
lessons.blurb: Switch tabs, maximize a window, try layout presets, and change the panel skin.

chapters.text: The screen is four windows: left, center, right, and bottom. Each one holds tabs, like a desktop editor.
The tab strip names what each window shows. Here: the Patch Bay, the Renderer, the Controls, and the Timeline.
The arrow button in a window's corner maximizes it. Click it again to restore.
The Window menu has layout presets. Tall stacks everything into one column.
Default brings back the four-window layout.
Under View, pick a skin. CRT is flat and compact. Hardware turns sliders into knobs. Rack, the default, adds patch cables.
Control plus and Control minus change the text size. Control zero resets it.
Rearrange freely. Reset Layout, in the Window menu, always brings you home. Next: sources.

lessons.title: Sources
lessons.blurb: Pattern Generator kinds, and loading a video file as the picture.

chapters.text: Every picture starts with a source. You can pick one on the start screen, or any time in the Source section of the Controls.
Open the Synth tab. Source is near the top.
The Pattern Generator makes pictures with no camera at all. Change its Kind to try another pattern. Lissajous.
Spiral. And Worley cells. Each kind brings its own controls, just below.
To use your own footage, choose a video file. Webcam, screen capture, and stream URLs work the same way.
The pattern was covering the whole picture, so loading a video switched it off. This is the video alone.
Turn the pattern back on, and set Blend to Screen. Now both show through.
Any source can feed the raster. Next, we will find our way around the Controls panel.

lessons.title: Finding your way around
lessons.blurb: Tabs, sections, search, knobs, ranges, and the ⓘ help.

chapters.text: The Controls panel holds every parameter, in three tabs. Synth shapes the picture.
I O connects MIDI, audio, OSC, and control voltage. Help holds the manual. Back to Synth.
Each tab is a stack of sections. Click a header to fold a section open or closed.
To find anything fast, press slash, or click the search box, and type. Bloom.
Drag a knob up or down to change it. Hold Shift for fine control. Double-click to reset it.
The small arrow by a knob opens its menu: type an exact value, widen the knob's range, or reset.
The i button on a section header explains it, and draws what is patched into it right now.
Press Escape in the search box to clear it, and everything folds back the way it was.
Next, we will use these controls to shape the raster itself.

lessons.title: Shaping the raster
lessons.blurb: Size, depth, rotation and luminance — the scan processor itself.

chapters.text: The Display Control Unit is the scan processor itself. It decides where every line is drawn.
H Size and V Size stretch the raster. H Position and V Position slide it around.
Z Push is depth: how far bright areas lift toward you. Z Bias moves the whole sheet forward or back.
Rotation turns the raster in its own plane.
V Spin turns it around its vertical axis.
Threshold hides the darkest parts of the picture, so only the brighter areas draw.
Intensity sets the brightness of the beam. Focus softens or sharpens it.
Double-click any knob to put it back. Next: color, glow, and presets.

lessons.title: Color, glow and presets
lessons.blurb: Bloom, feedback, the virtual camera, and one-click presets.

chapters.text: Color and Post FX change how the beam looks on screen, after the scan processor has drawn it.
Color Mode picks the phosphor. Amber, like an old terminal. Then back to green.
Bloom is the phosphor glow. Push the intensity for a hot, blown-out beam.
Burn-In Feedback leaves trails, like slow phosphor. Turn it on, and move the camera to see them.
In Virtual Camera, Field of View works like a zoom lens.
Presets apply a whole look at once. Heavy Bloom. Lissajous Scope. Classic 1974.
Mix and match, then save your own look in the Presets section. Next: modulation.

lessons.title: Modulation
lessons.blurb: A Classic modulation slot: a sine wave moving a parameter.

chapters.text: Modulation moves parameters for you, so the picture keeps changing on its own. Open the Modulation section.
Classic mode has four slots. Each is a function generator: a source, a target, and an amount.
Slot one's source is already a sine wave. Set its target to Z Push.
Switch the slot on.
Amount is how far it swings. Turn it up, and the raster starts to breathe.
Expand the slot for more. Rate sets how fast the wave cycles, in hertz.
This slot also appears in the Patch Bay as Function Generator one. Next: the Timeline.

lessons.title: Keyframes
lessons.blurb: Create a timeline, key a parameter at two bars, and play it back.

chapters.text: The Timeline, along the bottom, plays changes back over time, locked to the tempo.
Click New to make a timeline. It is sixteen bars long, at one hundred twenty beats per minute.
Click the ruler to move the playhead. Bar one.
Every knob has a small diamond above it. Click Z Push's diamond to set a keyframe at the playhead.
Move to bar three, and turn Z Push up. Once a parameter has a lane, every change is keyed automatically.
The lane below draws the curve, in the same numbers as the knob.
Press Play. The depth rises from bar one to bar three, holds, and the timeline loops.
Key as many parameters as you like. Next: scenes, which capture a whole look at once.

lessons.title: Scenes
lessons.blurb: Snapshot whole looks as scenes and let the timeline move between them.

chapters.text: Scenes capture every setting at once. The timeline blends from one scene to the next.
Double-click the Scenes track near the start, to capture the current look.
Now change the look. Apply the Amber Terminal preset, and push the depth.
Double-click at bar four, to capture the second scene.
Rewind, and press Play. The picture travels from the first look to the second.
Right-click a scene marker to preview it, replace its snapshot, or change its easing.
Keyframes and scenes work together on one timeline. Next: the Patch Bay.

lessons.title: Cables
lessons.blurb: Waveforms into a function generator, its output into a parameter; move and unplug.

chapters.text: The Patch Bay is the whole instrument as one hardware faceplate. Maximize it to see more.
Along the top, the Sources bus offers signals: waveforms, audio, beats, MIDI, and more. Every parameter has an input jack, a knob, and an output jack.
Cables run from an output to an input. Drag the triangle wave toward the bottom edge, and the board scrolls with you. Drop it on Function Generator one, the same slot as in the Modulation panel.
Now its output. Grab the output jack, and carry it up to H Size.
Restore the window. The raster now stretches in and out with the triangle wave.
Back in the bay, grab a cable by its input end to move it. Drop it on V Size.
Drop a cable in empty space to unplug it.
Cables and the Modulation panel are two views of one patch. Next: nodes.

lessons.title: Nodes and the Scope
lessons.blurb: Add nodes with a right-click, watch signals on a Scope, delete what you do not need.

chapters.text: Nodes are extra modules: oscillators, envelopes, logic, and more. Right-click empty board space to add one. An LFO.
Add a Scope beside it. A scope draws whatever signal passes through it.
Drag the LFO's output into the Scope's input. There's the wave.
The Scope passes its signal on. Patch its output into Z Push, and the raster follows the wave.
Turn the LFO's rate knob, and watch the trace speed up.
To remove a node, click its X and confirm. Its cables go with it.
Every node type is listed in the Node Catalog on the About page. Next: routing video.

lessons.title: Video routing
lessons.blurb: Composite a video file with the Pattern Generator and feed the renderer.

chapters.text: The Patch Bay also routes the picture itself. Video cables are magenta.
Load a video into Video Source A, with its File button.
Open its preview to check that it is playing.
Now patch the Pattern Generator's video output into Composite's B input.
Set the Composite blend to Screen, so both pictures show.
Finally, patch Composite's output into the Renderer's input.
Restore the window. The raster now carries both pictures at once.
Video Source B and Dual Raster patch the same way. From here, everything is one cable away.
